changelog:
Initial release with expanded context-aware commit message formatting.

- Follows the Conventional Commits specification with enforced ticket number and project tag when possible.
- Adds logic to extract ticket numbers from the current branch name.
- Auto-detects project type (API, CLIENT, CONSOLE, DB) from file paths in the diff; includes project tag only when determinable.
- Commit message headers include ticket number and/or project tag when available; omits them if unavailable.
- Enforces rules on message formatting, type matching the actual diff, and body usage.
- SKILL.md rewritten for clarity; sample skill-card.md removed.
summary: Write git commit messages following the Conventional Commits specification, with an automatic ticket number pulled from the current branch and a project tag (API / CLIENT / CONSOLE / DB) when the project type can be detected from the diff. Use this skill whenever the user asks to write a commit message, asks for help committing changes, runs `git commit`, or mentions writing changelog entries — even if they don't explicitly say "conventional commits".
